title: Tabi
pitch: One place for a group trip's plan, people and money. It's phone-first and invite-only, and it never shows a guess as if it were money already spent.
description: Case study: Tabi, a phone-first group trip planner designed and built solo by Tyler Crump, covering money states, privacy decisions and iteration.
contribution: Designed three money states (paid, committed, estimated) that always add up to the projected total, so a guess never reads as money already spent.
facts: Mobile-first web app, installable to the Home Screen

cover.alt: Tabi sign-in screen: a navy app icon with a red seal showing the character 旅, above the word Tabi in a serif typeface.
cover.caption: The public sign-in screen. Trip and account data stay private.

quick.label: The product
quick.text: A group trip planner for any trip, group size or budget. A Japan trip was its first real use.

quick.label: My part
quick.text: Everything: product design, interface, and the Express/SQLite build.

quick.label: Evidence
quick.text: A live app and four documented decisions with their reasons. It went through four iterations in 60 small pull requests over eight days.

sections.title: Certain money and guessed money never blur.
sections.intro: Every cost is marked paid, committed (booked but not fully paid) or estimated. The three always add up to the projected total. If no budget is set, the app says “No budget set” rather than inventing a figure.
sections.note: Illustration of the rule, not real trip data.

sections.title: Four decisions, and the reason for each.

items.title: Never show a guess as if it were certain
items.goal: Keep one planner flexible across trips, group sizes and budgets without blurring money that is certain with money that is a guess.
items.decision: Three money states on every cost, always summing to the projected total, with an honest “No budget set” state.
items.implementation: Added in the “precise money states” iteration and carried through the plan views.
items.effect: Money a group has spent and money it might spend lead to different decisions. Mixing them hides risk.

items.title: Gates, honestly
items.constraint: Airports assign gates a few hours before departure.
items.decision: Make the gate a field filled in on the day through a deliberately small form, and record when it was set.
items.implementation: A live-status link sits beside it. Flights without a number say so instead of showing a dead button.
items.effect: The app doesn't pretend to know. A gate from yesterday is worse than no gate at all.

items.title: Hide what could be misused
items.constraint: A booking reference plus a surname is often enough to change or cancel a booking.
items.decision: Guests see a flight's route, times, terminal and gate, but never the fare, seat or booking reference.
items.effect: Sharing a trip with the group doesn't mean sharing control of its bookings.

items.title: Invite-only, with Google sign-in
items.goal: The app holds a private group's plans and payments, so nobody should be able to wander in.
items.alternatives: Password sign-in and Apple Sign In were both tried. Apple was removed, then sign-in was made Google-only.
items.decision: Accounts are created only from an invite a trip owner issues.
items.effect: Each trip's group is closed by default, with viewer and editor roles.

sections.title: Four iterations, in small steps.
sections.intro: I iterated in small pull requests: 60 over eight days, 57 of them merged.
items: Feature build-out: a budget against a group target, live currency conversion (the Japan trip used AUD and JPY), a Today view and maps.
A budget-first, mobile-first redesign, then a full visual redesign.
Design pass: trip pass, departure board, route strip, payments to approve.
Precise money states, honest empty states, trips on their own clock and daily backups.
sections.gap: Before-and-after screens and tester feedback aren't published yet; the live app holds private trip data.

sections.title: Features.
items: More than one trip per account, each with its own invite-only group and viewer/editor roles.
A day-by-day itinerary with map pins.
A budget with a whole-group / per-person toggle and a budget-ceiling warning.
Live currency conversion and trip weather.
A home screen that shows a countdown before the trip and Today's plan during it.
A bottom bar per section and a single + that adds anything from anywhere.
A “Still to sort” check listing only what needs a look, and a “What changed?” line after each edit.
